root_cause.text: Lock ordering inversion between `device_lock` and `rfkill_global_mutex` in `nfc_unregister_device()` creates an ABBA deadlock when `rfkill_unregister()` is called while holding `device_lock`, since concurrent `rfkill_fop_write()` acquires these locks in the opposite order.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `rfkill_unregister()` and `rfkill_destroy()` outside the `device_lock` critical section by storing the rfkill pointer in a local variable (`rfk`) before releasing the lock, then calling these functions after `device_unlock()`. This eliminates the lock ordering inversion: Thread A (`rfkill_fop_write`) acquires `rfkill_global_mutex` then `device_lock`, while Thread B (`nfc_unregister_device`) now acquires only `device_lock` in its critical section, then `rfkill_global_mutex` after releasing `device_lock`, preventing the circular wait condition.

relevance_review.reason: The group addresses a potential use-before-initialization or null-dereference issue through variable initialization. The vulnerability root cause is a lock ordering inversion (ABBA deadlock) between `device_lock` and `rfkill_global_mutex`. These are distinct issues - one is about memory safety (null pointer), the other is about synchronization/deadlock. Initializing a variable to NULL does not resolve the lock ordering problem that causes the deadlock.

This group directly addresses the lock ordering inversion vulnerability by moving rfkill cleanup operations (which call rfkill_unregister()) outside the device_lock critical section. This eliminates the ABBA deadlock scenario where device_lock is held while acquiring rfkill_global_mutex, preventing the lock ordering inversion with concurrent rfkill_fop_write() operations.

NFC: RFKILL support

All NFC devices will now get proper RFKILL support as long as they provide
some dev_up and dev_down
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit be055b2f89b5842f41363b5655a33dffb51a8294
Author: Samuel Ortiz <sameo@linux.intel.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 11 11:52:20 2013 +0200

    NFC: RFKILL support
    
    All NFC devices will now get proper RFKILL support as long as they provide
    some dev_up and dev_down hooks. Rfkilling an NFC device will bring it down
    while it is left to userspace to bring it back up when being rfkill unblocked.
    This is very similar to what Bluetooth does.
    
    Acked-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtm
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `nfc_unregister_device()` function. At lines 893-896, `rfkill_unregister(dev->rfkill)` is called BEFORE acquiring `device_lock(&dev->dev)` (which happens later at line 899). However, the `nfc_rfkill_set_block()` callback (lines 126-139) calls `nfc_dev_down(dev)`, which internally acquires `device_lock(&dev->dev)` at line 60. This creates a lock ordering inversion: nfc_unregister_device holds no lock while calling rfkill_unregister, but rfkill_unregister can trigger rfkill_fop_write which calls nfc_rfkill_set_block, which then tries to acquire device_lock. Meanwhile, nfc_unregister_device later acquires device_lock at line 899. If rfkill_unregister internally acquires rfkill_global_mutex and then device_lock is held elsewhere, an ABBA deadlock occurs. The fix would require holding device_lock before calling rfkill_unregister, or restructuring the lock acquisition order to prevent the inversion.
